subject: MediCore renewal + EU residency + APAC pilot — SOW and next steps
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@medicore.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Renewal discussion — EU residency requirement & APAC pilot

Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. MediCore is approaching the end of our current contract window and the execs have signaled a strong preference to formalize EU data residency as part of the renewal. We also want to scope a limited APAC pilot (warm standby) to support our Singapore customers later this year.

High level asks from our side:
- Move primary production for EU traffic to an EU-resident node (data at rest + logs stay in EU).
- APAC pilot: warm standby with failover for latency-sensitive flows (initial 2 GPUs, scale plan).
- Clarify cross-region failover SLA and egress behavior when failover occurs.
- Term: open to 12–24 month options; need pricing impact and any discounts for committed capacity.

Can Redwood share an updated SOW and indicative pricing so we can review with procurement? Also please include SOC2 evidence and KMS options for key management.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Liu
Head of Procurement, MediCore
[sara.liu@medicore.com]

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — EU residency requirement & APAC pilot

Sara —

Appreciate the clarity. We'll put together a targeted renewal proposal that includes: an EU resident primary deployment plan, an APAC warm-standby pilot configuration, and explicit failover behavior (including any egress/charging implications).

Quick asks from our side to make the SOW precise:
- Target EU go-live window (Q3 or Q4 2027?)
- Expected average and peak RPS (requests per second) and token profile for EU traffic so we can size the pool and estimate costs
- Preferred term (12 vs 24 months) and whether you want a committed GPU pool or a reserved spend commitment

I’ve looped in Marissa (account lead) for the SOW draft and Grace (customer success) for runbook and onboarding details. We’ll aim to have a draft SOW + pricing by Monday.

Best —

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@medicore.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:45:00 +0000
Subject: Draft SOW & pricing (MediCore renewal) — attachments included

Sara / Ben —

Attached is a first-pass SOW (redwood_sow_medicore_v1.pdf) and a pricing workbook (pricing_breakdown_medicore.xlsx). Highlights:

- Scope: EU primary tenancy (data residency for in-region compute + logs retained in-region), APAC warm standby (2x GPU initial, autoscale policy available), cross-region failover routing with automated prefix caching preserved where possible.
- Suggested term: 24 months recommended to lock unit pricing and get 12% volume discount on committed capacity. 12-month option also shown.
- Capacity: baseline reserved pool sized for 600 RPS equivalent EU workload with burstable headroom to 1,200 RPS; APAC pilot configured as hot-standby with pre-warmed nodes to keep failover latency below 350ms on average.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II package included; customer-managed KMS supported for EU tenant (we’ll provide KMS integration checklist).
- SLAs: 99.9% uptime on dedicated pool; specific failover SLAs included in section 4.3 (subject to final topology).

Open items called out in the SOW: exact RPS/token profiles, preferred KMS provider (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / HSM), and procurement contact for redlines.

Attachments: redwood_sow_medicore_v1.pdf (PDF), pricing_breakdown_medicore.xlsx (XLSX)

Planning note: if you confirm the 24-month term and committed capacity, we can carve an EU-resident node in our Q3 provisioning window and schedule a staged cutover with a test failover.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@medicore.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 14:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Draft SOW & pricing (MediCore renewal) — a few redlines

Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed the SOW and attached a redlines doc (medicore_redlines.docx) — high-level items below:
- Confirmed: MediCore prefers a 24-month committed term if the 12% discount applies and if failover egress is charged at capped rate.
- Redline: need clearer definition of "data residency" — does "logs" include aggregated telemetry exported for product analytics? If so, we need an opt-in for exports outside EU.
- Redline: request explicit egress cap (monthly) for failover events to avoid unbounded charges during sustained incident.
- Contracting ask: deviation in payment terms (Net 60) and procurement signature block for MediCore legal.

I’ve inserted comments in the redlines doc. Can you confirm whether the KMS model supports customer key rotation without impacting token cache encryption? Also send the SOC2 package and any penetration test reports you can share under NDA.

On timing: procurement wants the final SOW and commercial terms by July 6 to hit the renewal cycle.

Best —
Sara

Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 15:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Draft SOW & pricing (MediCore renewal) — next steps and timeline

Sara —

Thanks for the detailed review and the redlines. Action plan and responses below:

1) Term & discount: We can commit to the 24-month term with the 12% committed-capacity discount as long as the committed GPU pool aligns to the baseline in the pricing workbook. I’ll add a clause for egress capping during failover events (proposal: a $X/GB cap for first 72 hours; details in revised SOW).

2) Data residency / logs: By default telemetry aggregation used for product analytics is anonymized and flagged for opt-in exports. We’ll add an explicit export opt-in toggle for EU tenants and call this out in the SOW. No logs will be exported outside EU unless explicitly enabled by MediCore.

3) KMS & cache: Customer KMS rotation is supported; rotating keys will not invalidate the KV/token cache — we maintain a wrapping key approach and will document the rotation process in the KMS checklist.

4) Deliverables & timeline:
- Revised SOW + redline responses (Marissa) — Jul 2 EOD
- SOC2 + pentest artifacts (NDA required) — Grace to coordinate (expect 2 business days after NDA)
- Final commercial term sheet and DocuSign envelope — Jul 5
- EU node provision window: Q3 provisioning (aiming for deploy week of Aug 16)
- APAC pilot: ready to standby two weeks post EU deploy, run 6-week pilot, then review scale targets.

5) Procurement terms: We can accept Net 60 with standard onboarding milestone invoice schedule — legal to confirm final language.

Next steps: I’ll attach the revised SOW and update pricing caps per Sara’s ask. Please confirm an exec review slot next week (I can book a 30-min call with Evan and our Head of Product to walk the topology). HubSpot deal: HS-9876543. DocuSign (prelim): https://docusign.net/envelope/ABC123456

If that aligns, Marissa will push the updated PDF and the pricing workbook with the egress cap numbers attached.

Regards —
